Subject: Clarify: backup purge timelines + EU transfer for AcmeHealth

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Compliance asked me to confirm a few items before we move to procurement:

- We need a clear backup purge schedule — specifically how long backups are retained after a user delete request and whether there is a separate "backup purge" timeline versus the primary datastore retention.
- Does Redwood perform any cross-border transfer of logs/backups that may contain personal data (EU -> US)? If so, what safeguards / SCCs / DPA clauses cover those transfers?
- Request: a "subprocessor passport" (CSV with subprocessor name, country, purpose, SOC2 cert link) — our legal team will use it to validate suppliers.
- Finally, can Redwood offer an exception window for log retention during a live investigation (we typically ask for a 30d forensic hold option)?

Could you send a short timeline and an updated DPA addendum we can share with legal? We need something internal by EOD Friday (30 Apr).

Appreciate it —
Olivia

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I'll loop in Legal for DPA redlines and send a draft addendum by tomorrow.

1) Backup purge schedule: our standard pipeline removes deleted user data from primary storage within 24 hours, but backups are retained on a rolling snapshot schedule. Backups that may contain deleted records are purged on a 90-day cadence by default; we can offer a customer-specific 60-day cadence under committed contracts.

2) Cross-border transfers: we do route backups and operational logs through our EU-hosted storage (primary), but we replicate aggregated metrics to US for platform analytics. Personal-data-containing backups are kept in-region unless a customer explicitly requests cross-border processing. We support SCCs + standard DPA clauses; we also offer a Private deployment (VPC) if strict data residency is required.

3) Subprocessor passport: attaching a current export (CSV) — it lists subprocessors, country, purpose and links to SOC2 reports where available.

4) Forensic hold: we can enable a one-time 30-day investigation hold on relevant logs/backups for security incidents. We treat this as an exception and require a signed MPA (mutual action plan) that documents scope, retention start/end, and audit access.

I'll attach a DPA addendum draft and a short mutual-action-plan template; Kimberly from Legal will provide the redlines.

Best,

Ben —

Thanks for the heads up. Quick redlines and guidance below (I tracked high-level changes so Sales can push to Acme):

- Backup purge: we can offer a contractual option for 60-day purge of snapshot backups that might contain deleted records. Wording: "Redwood will purge customer snapshot backups that may contain deleted customer data within 60 days of deletion unless otherwise agreed in writing." This preserves the default 90d for self-serve customers.

- Cross-border transfers: include a clause that "Personal-data-containing backups and system logs will be retained and processed in the EU by default. Redwood may process aggregated, pseudonymized operational metrics in other jurisdictions for platform maintenance and analytics; no raw personal data will be transferred without Customer consent or lawful basis (e.g., SCCs)." Add reference to SCCs and Data Transfer Impact Assessment in an Annex.

- Forensic hold: we will provide a one-time 30-day forensic hold on specified datasets upon Customer request and execution of a Mutual Action Plan. Wording to add: maximum two forensic-hold requests per rolling 12 months; Redwood reserves the right to charge for extraordinary retrieval/retention work at our then-current rates. This limits operational exposure.

- Subprocessor passport: fine to provide CSV. Add an attestation line: "Subprocessors listed have been informed and maintain applicable certifications to the best of Redwood's knowledge." We should not warrant continuous SOC2 status; instead provide links and last-checked dates.

I'll attach a redlined addendum v2 for you to send to Acme. Karthik, can you confirm whether backups are encrypted with customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private tiers? I'll add the KMS/HSM note.

kimberly
